text: Goal: cut this agent's eval loop from hours to minutes.
Asking myself: where does the wall-clock actually live?
→ run_history(suite='eval', last_n=30)
Almost all of it is one serial stage. Worth zooming in.
→ profile_stage(name='context_build')
Every case rebuilds the same context from scratch. Cache it once, reuse everywhere.
→ propose_change(target='context_build', strategy='shared_cache')
Cache stays well under the memory ceiling. Looks safe.
→ dry_run(branch='perf/context-cache', sample=0.1)
Sample finishes in seconds against a minutes-long baseline. Shipping it.
→ open_pr(title='context_build: shared cache across eval cases')
Eval loop down from hours to minutes. Awaiting review.
Next request: an agent fails silently when its input queue is empty.
→ read_logs(agent='triage', last='6h', filter='warn|error')
No errors logged — just an empty result loop. Classic.
→ add_guard(agent='triage', condition='len(batch) == 0', action='alert')
→ write_test(name='triage_empty_queue', expect='alert + skip')
Guard wired in, test passes, alert fires in under 2s.
Standardizing harness boilerplate across three agents — let's diff them first.
→ compare_skeletons(['router', 'retriever', 'evaluator'])
Same setup block repeated three times. Lifting to a shared module.
→ refactor(extract='harness.bootstrap', shared_between=3)
Three agents now share one bootstrap. -340 lines, +1 test file.
